messages:
tara: FYI discovered a parity/precedence snafu between SDKs when running the sample-app in the dev container. Node SDK used netrc (legacy file) over the env var I set, but Python SDK used the env var. CI injects ORG_API_KEY which made the local .env PROJECT_KEY invisible in node. Super confusing.

ben: Yikes. Can you show the repro steps and the effective header that hit the backend?

tara: Minimal repro: start dev container -> mount repo with .env (contains REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY) -> shell exports ORG_API_KEY in CI. Node behavior (observed): picks netrc if present, then ORG env, then project env. Python: env > netrc. Example headers from my curl: 

```
POST /v1/complete
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer org_live_abc",
  "X-Redwood-Project": "proj_live_def"
}
Status: 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"project key not authorized for org-only route"}
```

ben: So both headers were sent? Or did netrc return a different header name?

tara: Node SDK attaches netrc token as Authorization, then picks up ORG_API_KEY as fallback; project key is added as X-Redwood-Project by the sample app (legacy behavior). The backend rejects because it expects a single token.

lee: Two separate issues: 1) SDK source precedence mismatch across languages; 2) sample-app adding legacy project header when org token present. For (1) we should standardize precedence and ship tests across SDKs. I propose canonical precedence: explicit SDK param > CLI flag > env var (REDWOOD_*) > netrc > legacy files.

ben: Agreed on standardizing. Also we should expose metadata on outgoing requests so we can diagnose in logs: add header `X-Auth-Source: env|netrc|flag|param` and `X-Auth-Used: org|project` in dev/debug builds only. That would have saved a lot of time.

tara: Love the X-Auth-Source idea. Also please prevent sample-app from bundling a checked-in .env by default. Add .env.example and ensure Dockerfile doesn't COPY .env. I hit this exact footgun.

ops-bot: build-failure: sample-app / integration-test #9245 failed in CI at step "e2e run" (1751112200).

lee: For streaming APIs we must be careful: if we swap auth mid-stream the server must support resume. Not all routes do. Plan: SDK should not auto-send multiple auth headers. If conflicting keys found, emit a single deterministic warning and pick the highest-precedence token. If the server returns 401, invoke onAuthRefresh hook before tearing down stream.

ben: Implementation checklist for SDKs: 
- Add AuthSource enum + unified precedence documented in repo docs
- Add `--auth-source` CLI override (explicit)
- Emit `WARN` once per process if conflicting sources detected (rate-limit to 1/min)
- Add optional debug headers `X-Auth-Source` behind DEV flag
- Add inter-SDK conformance tests (node <-> python) for precedence and streaming 401 handling

doc-bot: note: add entry to devex docs: "Auth resolution and precedence (env, netrc, cli, params)" and update sample-app README to call out removing .env in Dockerfile.

tara: One more: rotation. CI rotates org keys nightly; if a job runs across rotation and netrc caches older creds, flaky 401s appear. Suggest cache invalidation on 403 for cached netrc tokens and a small backoff retry to pick up new env-injected key.

lee: Good call. On 403 if auth-source==cache/netrc, invalidate and re-resolve sources, then retry once. If still failing, surface an actionable error ("legacy credentials invalid; try `redwood auth login` or set REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY").

ben: I'll draft a tiny SDK RFC + unit test harness for parity tests. Tara, can you open a PR to remove .env from the sample Dockerfile and add .env.example? That will reduce accidental commits.

tara: Opening PR now, will include repro steps and a short log snippet. cc @dev-tools. Thanks all! :rocket:
